doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Recording output and small-label pay
summary: About 125 recordings; small labels pay flat fees with little residual income.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: You’ve been on a lot of records already.
Yeah. I think it’s something like 125 counting videos and audio tapes and CDs and things like that.
With the small labels, they pretty much pay you a set fee for your session?

Yeah. You have to be on RCA or Sony, CBS, Verve, something like that, to get any kind of residual. I’ve gotten payments from the Recording Manufacturer’s Fund, but that’s the only kind of residual I ever get, unless I buy product at a discount and re-sell it on the job. Then you can make a little more that way. We get an artist discount when we buy our CD, so we’re not paying full price. But still, we may have to play a local tax on it, or pay someone to handle it, so by the time I wind up with $7.50 to split five ways, none of us are getting rich on a CD sale.

But I’ll keep making them anyway. I mean I’ve made some I’m really, really proud of and in all different styles that I can play. I’ve done just about every drum style that I can play. A couple I’ve missed, but I imagine I’ll get to them.
